patches.old: The value $\zeta(s)$ is the tip-to-tail sum of infinitely many shrinking arrows spinning at incommensurate rates. A zero of $\zeta$ is a value of $s$ at which all these arrows add up to exactly nothing.
patches.new: The value $\zeta(s)$ is the tip-to-tail sum of infinitely many shrinking arrows spinning at different rates $\log k$. (These rates are not all incommensurate, since $\log4=2\log2$ and $\log6=\log2+\log3$. It is the rates $\log p$ of distinct primes that are mutually incommensurate, a fact used in Chapter~\ref{ch:fourier-series} and proved for $p=2,3$ in Problem 26.) Where the sum converges ($\sigma>1$) the arrows never cancel completely; we prove this in \cref{sec:zeta-euler}. The zeros we want lie where this sum diverges, and making sense of them is the job of analytic continuation (\cref{sec:zeta-continuation}).

patches.new:
It involves the Gamma function, which we now recall (Chapter~\ref{ch:asymptotics} treats it more fully). For $\Re z>0$ it is defined by
\[
\Gamma(z)=\int_0^\infty x^{z-1}e^{-x}\,\dd x,\qquad x^{z-1}=e^{(z-1)\log x}.
\]
Integrate by parts with $u=x^{z}$ and $\dd v=e^{-x}\,\dd x$. The derivative formula proved in the lemma of \cref{sec:zeta-continuation} gives $\frac{\dd}{\dd x}x^{z}=z\,x^{z-1}$, so
\[
\Gamma(z+1)=\Bigl[-x^{z}e^{-x}\Bigr]_0^\infty+z\int_0^\infty x^{z-1}e^{-x}\,\dd x=z\,\Gamma(z).
\]
The boundary term vanishes because $|x^{z}|=x^{\Re z}\to0$ as $x\to0$, and because $e^{-x}$ decays faster than any power grows as $x\to\infty$. Since $\Gamma(1)=\int_0^\infty e^{-x}\,\dd x=1$, repeated use of $\Gamma(z+1)=z\,\Gamma(z)$ gives $\Gamma(n+1)=n!$ for $n=0,1,2,\dots$. In this sense $\Gamma$ generalizes the factorial.

What, exactly, is proved? A computed sign can be trusted only when the computed $|Z|$ is larger than a guaranteed bound on the rounding and truncation error of the evaluation. The proof therefore uses two points where $|Z|$ is safely nonzero with opposite signs, for example $t=14$ and $t=15$. The intermediate value theorem then gives a zero of $Z$ between them, and hence a zero of $\zeta$ exactly on the critical line. Bisection refines the location, not the proof. Chapter 4 is now only a 'see also' reference: Gamma is recalled with its integral definition, and the recurrence is derived by integration by parts; bisection is described in words. In the Euler-product proof the integer sets are renamed to mathcal I_P and mathcal I_{P,J}, and the paired eta terms to D_j; partial sums keep the letter S. The Connes discussion now defers to his own proof and drops the guessed sign-change mechanism; Problem 24 is reworded to match. The CHECKS script gains five things: a grid sign-change count (Problem 19), the |zeta(rho_n)|<1e-17 check (Answer 17), the 19-digit t_1 string, the t_10000<1e4 check, and the spacing 0.852 at t=1e4 (revised Answer 21). It also adds numerical instances of the Gamma recurrence and of eta(0)=1/2. The geometric-series figure script was not provided, so the caption's 'shaded' region now refers to x<-1.
